description_block:
In Des mots sous les arbres, Etel Adnan unfolds one of the most intimate and emblematic forms of her practice: the leporello, the accordion-fold book that allows painting and writing to enter into dialogue. On Japanese paper, the artist alternates washes, ink, and handwritten signs, giving rise to vegetal silhouettes, calligraphic verticals, and fragments of language that seem to hover between landscape and poem. The work invites both reading and contemplation, unfolding a continuous rhythm. Conceived as a visual promenade, the elongated format places temporality at the very heart of the composition.
This piece fully reflects Etel Adnanâs artistic approach, that of a major figure of Mediterranean and cosmopolitan modernity. A poet before she was a painter, Adnan always conceived painting as an extension of writing, and writing as an extension of painting, in search of a visual language capable of capturing the experience of the world, nature, and exile. Leporellos occupy a central place in this exploration, at the crossroads of book art, calligraphy, and lyrical abstraction. Des mots sous les arbres thus stands as a rare synthesis of pictorial gesture and poetic thought, affirming Etel Adnan as one of the most singular and celebrated voices in contemporary international art.

description_block:
The duo Arotin & Serghei is devoted to the exploration of infinity and to the transgression of boundaries between painting, sound, light, and space. Their opus magnum Infinite Screen unfolds within emblematic contexts such as the Venice Biennale, the Kunsthistorisches Museum, the Fondation Beyeler, and the Centre Pompidou. In Metamorphosis 3, the work is structured around two parallel piano strings tuned to 330 Hz, corresponding to the note E. Though silent, these strings establish a conceptual and spatial field of resonance, translated visually through vibrations of color and light. The integrated prisms fragment and recombine the pigmented surfaces, generating an unstable chromatic fusion in constant transformation. Formally restrained, the work nonetheless initiates a profound reflection on art and the digital condition. Painting here becomes a perceptual device â a process and a temporal, sensory experience â in which infinity is conceived as a continuous metamorphosis from the visible toward the immaterial, engaging directly with the technological and philosophical questions of our time.
